AEClinicalPictureCounts.description:
Severity-bucketed counts from the AE clinical-picture LLM component.

Counts reflect *kept* findings only (i.e. after the dedup step
suppresses subordinate findings under a decisive global mismatch).
They are derivable from the master ``Inconsistency`` list by
filtering ``source == "llm_ae_clinical_picture"`` and
``suppressed is False``, but persisted explicitly for ergonomics
and downstream symmetry with ``ClinicalDateInconsistencyCounts``.

See: llm/tasks/ae_clinical_picture.py
AEClinicalPictureCounts.title: AEClinicalPictureCounts

AEClinicalPictureStatus.description:
Assessment status for the AE clinical-picture inconsistency component.

Distinguishes "the LLM assessed the AE pictures and produced findings"
from "no LLM assessment was performed" (no LLM client configured,
trivially-matched skip, or LLM error).  Downstream code must treat
``NOT_ASSESSED`` as *no information*, not as "assessed and found no
discrepancies".

The accompanying ``reason`` string (carried alongside the status on
``PairFeatures.ae_clinical_picture_reason``) refines ``NOT_ASSESSED``
into one of: ``""`` (assessed), ``"no_llm_client"``,
``"trivially_matched"``, or ``"llm_error"``.  Reason is a string
rather than an enum so new codes can be added without enum churn.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § AE clinical-picture inconsistency
AEClinicalPictureStatus.title: AEClinicalPictureStatus

Exposes the individual feature probabilities that are multiplied

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Probability estimation
FeatureContribution.title: FeatureContribution

Inconsistency.description:
A detected inconsistency between two reports.

Carries entries from all sources: rule-based demographic/drug-set
checks and LLM-assisted AE clinical-picture findings. The optional
``source``, ``kind``, ``rationale``, ``terms``, ``cluster_label``,
``suppressed`` and ``suppressed_by`` fields support the richer
LLM-derived entries while remaining backwards-compatible defaults
for existing rule-based call sites.

Suppressed entries (``suppressed=True``) are kept in the master
list for transparency in human review but are excluded from the
severity counts that feed downstream decision logic.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Inconsistency Detection
Inconsistency.title: Inconsistency

InconsistencyCounts.description:
Summary counts of inconsistencies by severity level.

These counts are merged across all inconsistency sources:
demographic (age, weight, height, sex), drug-set, clinical-date,
and narrative-derived inconsistencies.  They feed directly into
the weighted inconsistency score w_tot in the decision logic.

Decisive inconsistencies (e.g. distinct patient IDs from the
same study, or clinical-date impossibilities) contribute to
w_tot via ``w_decisive``, which is set high enough that any
decisive count always exceeds the zone tolerance.
InconsistencyCounts.title: InconsistencyCounts

InconsistencySeverity.description:
Severity levels for detected inconsistencies between reports.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Severity Levels

Levels:
    minor     – small difference, weakly suggests different individuals
    moderate  – meaningful difference, weakens the duplicate hypothesis
    strong    – strongly suggests different individuals
    decisive  – forces Different classification (e.g. distinct
                patient IDs from the same study in the narratives)
InconsistencySeverity.title: InconsistencySeverity

NarrativeConsistency.description:
Narrative consistency categories from LLM assessment.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Narrative Consistency Assessment

Values
------
STRONGLY_CONSISTENT : narratives clearly describe the same patient
CONSISTENT : probable but not certain match
NEUTRAL : narratives too sparse to judge
INCONSISTENT : narratives clearly describe different patients
NOT_AVAILABLE : LLM assessment was not performed or failed
NarrativeConsistency.title: NarrativeConsistency
